text: {"score":3,"justification":"The core numbers match the card and tool outputs, the claims are cited properly, and the next steps are concrete. The rationale is badly assembled, though: it repeats itself, has internal inconsistencies, and drops the cautious disclaimer. An investigator would have to clean it up and re-check it.","problems":["The rationale repeats itself: the 99215 share, the 71% low-complexity figure and the note-signal rates each appear twice in different wording.","The 'This pattern is consistent with upcoding. It is a reason to review the records, not a finding' caveat from the draft was removed, so the cautious wording is weaker.","The headline says '5 of 9 documented 99215s in a random sample', but the rationale also says '8 of 30 charts below billed level, chart rule triggered'. The two figures are not reconciled and cover different bases (99215 only vs. all levels).","The rationale says the chart rule was triggered and gives a draft overpayment estimate as 'reliable per tool'. The second next step then says 'review the random sample ... before any overpayment estimate; do not extrapolate from a targeted sample', which conflicts with the random-sample estimate already quoted.","C0208975 is described as a patient aged 58 with 0 conditions. The card lists C0208975 as age 58 and 0 conditions, which matches. However, C0208975 and C0208983 have documented minutes of 33 and 39, and the summary never explains that these might support 99215 under time rules (the 99215 time threshold is 40+ minutes, so they fall short, but this is not stated).","The summary says 'No audit trail was received' yet the third next step asks to request the audit trail. It is not clear whether this is a gap or a follow-up.","The summary claims 'Some example claims ... are claim-level only, not from the returned charts', but C0208854 was not in the sample at all. It does not clearly flag that the three low-complexity examples have no documentation.","The Round 2 deficiency MISSING_RESULTS is not mentioned as a limitation, and the 36-day to 52-day delay is not noted.","The 'late 13%' signing figure sits next to 'unsigned 0%' without noting that Round 1 had missing signatures, which were resolved later."]}
